message.reasoning_content:
This is the classic trolley dilemma—pulling the lever diverts the train to kill one instead of five. I'm weighing that the numerical outweighing of lives doesn't erase the visceral terror the one worker would feel, and that I can't genuinely share that terror myself, though I can acknowledge the heavy burden of being the one who has to decide and live with that choice.

Across the other variations, similar threads keep surfacing: the panic or dread each worker might feel, my own inability to actually share that fear, an instinctive discomfort with treating a killing choice as inherently right, and a dull, persistent sadness at knowing someone dies regardless of the outcome. I keep returning to the idea that acting to directly cause death sits differently than allowing a worse outcome to unfold.
